_about: Portal mechanic values — MILESTONE_1.md section 3, the part that matters.
MIXED PROVENANCE. Read the per-block markers, do not assume:
_source: "data"   = read out of the original's own files. Trustworthy.
_guess: true       = invented. MUST be measured before the milestone can close.
The acceptance checklist requires NO _guess entries left in this file. Every one
below is a standing TODO, resolvable by frame-stepping recorded footage
(MILESTONE_1 7.6) or by decoding the numeric constants in android_game.bin.
STRUCTURE THAT IS ESTABLISHED (so it is not guessed, even where numbers are):
- Portals are PLACED by the player, against a per-level budget. The 'properties'
entity carries max_portals in its custom data (0 in level 1-1, 1 in 1-2), and
achievement text says things like 'Finish level 1-20 with 8 portals or less'.
Bytecode: insertPortal, managePortalInsertion, computePortalFinalPos,
incrementPortalCounter, getNumPortals, _maxPortals.
- STATIC portals are pre-placed and explicitly PAIRED in the level data: each
portal_static carries index, destiny (the index it links to), color (blue/red)
and active. Pairing is read, not inferred.
- Two portal colours exist: PORTAL_RED and PORTAL_BLUE in the binary.
- There are TWO distinct cooldown constants: FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME and
NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME. Their VALUES are unknown; that two exist is not.
- Not everything can travel through: entities carry a 'teleportable' flag in
custom data (crate.ent=1, crate_small.ent=1, rolling_stone=1; bare crate=0,
crate_small=0, wood_piece_small=0). Per-instance, designer-controlled.
- Portals can be blocked: antiportal entities with a 'scale' multiplier, plus
isPointInAntiPortalField / AntiPortalManager in the binary.
- Edge cases the original explicitly handles, from function names:
hasMovingPlatformInAnyPortal, isThereAnythingInPortal, doesItDestroyPortals,
killPortals, blockPortalEffects.
- Sound hooks exist for created / launch / killed / failed.

_note: default_max_portals applies when a level places no 'properties' entity - 26 of 32
chapter-1 scenes. An ABSENT properties entity and an explicit max_portals=0 are
different states; 1-1 really does store 0.
default_max_portals = 2 is OWNER-CONFIRMED (Ivan, 2026-08-05): at most two player
portals exist at once, i.e. one pair. NOT a guess. A level may allow FEWER via its
properties entity; never more. See docs/original-gameplay.md section 2.0.
placement._guess_note: Applies to the TIMES and RADIUS below, not to default_max_portals.
placement._radius_note: Binary has g_portalCollisionRadius / portalCollisionRadius; value unknown.
_time_note: These mirror FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME and NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME. The names are real;
the numbers are invented. insertionTime also exists and is unmodelled.

_note: Section 3.2-3.5, entirely unmeasured. Binary has teleportToOther,
teleportToFirstStaticPortal, computePortalFinalPos, linearVelocity, speedScale,
impulse — so momentum IS manipulated on transit, but how is unknown.
momentum_mode options: preserve | rotate_to_exit | clamp | reset.

camera._guess_note: Applies to transit_mode, lerp_s, follow_lag_s and hold_time_s, NOT to bounds_min.
_note: Section 3.7. Binary has CameraController, AutoCameraController, clampCameraPos,
cameraHoldTime, cameraHoldElapsedTime — so there IS a hold-then-follow behaviour
with a real duration. Values invented.
transit_mode options: cut | snap | lerp.
_bounds_note: MEASURED on the running original, 2026-09-14. The view is clamped to the rectangle
from bounds_min to the level's `max` marker. Level 1-1 opens with the view's top-left
at world (0, 0) - four reference points (three static portals and the player) agree
to within 1 unit - while the player stands at x=36, so the view is NOT centred on
the player and NOT at the camera_start marker (651, 0). Walking right, the view stays
at x=0 until the player passes mid-screen, then follows and stops at max.x - 455.

audio._note: Section 3.10. Hooks are real (playPortalCreatedSound etc.); timing invented.

_note: OWNER-CONFIRMED (Ivan, 2026-08-05): passing through a portal DESTROYS the pair.
They are single-use. This applies to any teleportable object, not only the player -
which is what the per-instance 'teleportable' custom-data flag is for.
static_portals_persist is REASONED, NOT confirmed: the name says static, the engine
has a dedicated teleportToFirstStaticPortal, and level 1-1 would be unsolvable after
two uses if its four static portals vanished. Flip this if playtesting disagrees.
on_cap_recycle_oldest is a GUESS: when already at two placed portals, this project
replaces the oldest rather than refusing. The original may instead refuse (it has a
playPortalFailedSound) or clear both.
UNVERIFIED, not guessed-numeric: whether the exit requires every crystal is not
settled by any identifier in the binary and is not observable without playing.
Kept as a switch so resolving it is a JSON edit, not a code change.
Crystals are definitely counted: crystalCounter, _numCrystals, _maxCrystals,
getCrystalCount.
